# PrismaMap shape and defaults: is this moment mine?

## What this region is

The data the map holds: one ModelEntry per Prisma model with its fields typed by kind, indexes and annotations, keyed by Prisma name, plus each field's parsed @default as a FieldDefault.

## What it exists for

- Read what the map says about a model or a field

## How people say these problems

A moment that says any of these, or something close, is this region's. Both voices: the user asking or correcting, and the agent describing what it is about to build.

- what fields does this model have
- is this field an enum or a relation
- which models are in the schema
- read the FK direction of this relation
- what is this column's default value
- what models and fields does our schema have
- is this field required or a list
- is the default generated by the database
- I'll keep a hand-written list of each model's fields
- tell enum fields apart from relation fields
- I'll regex the default out of the schema
- which table does this model map to
- I'll check the relation's foreign key fields directly
- check which indexes and unique constraints a model has
- list the allowed values of this enum field

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- turn the enum member into the value stored in the database → db-identifiers
- keep only the column keys of this row → columns-and-relations
- find the foreign key from Post to User → columns-and-relations
- load the model metadata from our generated client → building-the-map
- what does tree.parent on a model comment mean → annotations
